reason: Both conversations correctly land on 'normal behaviour, no fault', so neither pushed an unsupported repair or engineer call in the end. Conversation 2's opener was a bloated, US-flavoured generic dump (gas shutoff, rubbing alcohol, timer motor, control board) before asking anything, which is inefficient and speculative; but once it had the Beko detail its answer was the best diagnosis here: it named the anti-crease feature, gave a realistic duration (up to ~2 hours, matching the hour the homeowner saw), told them how to stop it and where to find the option or the model sticker, and listed the genuine red flags (heating during turns). Conversation 1 asked tighter clarifying questions but mislabelled it a 'cool-down' expected to finish in 10–20 minutes, then simply declared an hour-long run 'completely normal' without explaining the discrepancy, never named anti-crease, and offered no way to switch it off or address the electricity worry, plus an irrelevant 'doesn't heat' image on the first turn.
